title: Your weekly rule
hook: write your week on one page; Benedict spreads the psalms over a week and calls his Rule a little rule for beginners
tomorrow: a rabbi was ordered to break his own calendar. did he obey?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: play. David danced before the ark and wouldn't apologize. Today the weekly practices come together on one page.

A first weekly plan can look like a wall of colored blocks, every hour spoken for. Saint Benedict, writing his Rule for monks, had a heroic standard to measure against. The old monks, he writes, were said to sing the full hundred and fifty psalms in a single day. He doesn't ask that of his monks. He spreads the psalms over the whole week, and says: let us, lukewarm as we are, manage it in a week.
screen: `EVERY HOUR SPOKEN FOR.` → `ALL THE PSALMS IN ONE DAY?` → `LET US MANAGE IT IN A WEEK.`

segments.voice: That line opens up the whole Rule of Saint Benedict. Near its end he calls it a little rule written for beginners. It sets a rhythm, not a feat: prayer at fixed hours, work with the hands, set times for reading. Idleness, he writes, is the enemy of the soul, so the week has a shape. But he keeps making room inside it. Weak brothers get work that won't crush them. The old and the young are treated gently. And the abbot is told to arrange everything so the strong still have something to reach for and the weak don't run away. In Christian monastic life, a rule, regula in Latin, isn't a list of punishments. It's a frame a life can grow along. Benedictine monks and nuns still live by this one, and laypeople called oblates follow it outside the cloister. And notice the unit Benedict chose. Not the day. The week. Over seven days everything gets its turn: the psalms, the work, the reading. That's what a weekly rule can be. One page: your rest day, your service, your people, your outdoors, your study, your silence, your review, your screen-free stretch, your play, each with its day. Not everything every day. Everything in its week.
screen: `A LITTLE RULE FOR BEGINNERS.` · `ROOM FOR THE WEAK AND THE STRONG.` · `REGULA: A FRAME TO GROW ALONG.` · `EVERYTHING IN ITS WEEK.` · then, large: `MY WEEK.`

segments.voice: Take a sheet of paper and draw seven short lines, one for each day. Write your rest day in first, then the longer practices, one per line, wherever they fit. Leave at least one line nearly empty.
Your weekly rule: your week on one page, each practice on its day, built the way Benedict built his, for a beginner.
Keep this one: my week, built for a beginner, with the psalms spread out the way Benedict spread them. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Benedictine monks and nuns live by the Rule of Saint Benedict, with the psalms prayed across each week at fixed hours; oblates adapt it to ordinary lives. People writing their own weekly rule often fit it on one page, one line per day.
